title: Chapter1
description: Finnish vocabulary: personal information, greetings and basic verbs

questions.question: Signature
questions.explanation: 'Allekirjoitus' means signature, from 'alle' (under) and 'kirjoitus' (writing).
questions.exampletranslate: I need your signature on this agreement.

questions.question: Excuse me / Sorry
questions.explanation: 'Anteeksi' is used to say sorry or to get someone's attention.
questions.exampletranslate: Excuse me, where is the train station?

questions.question: To live (somewhere)
questions.explanation: 'Asua' (type 1 verb) means to live or reside, and is used with 'missä' (where).

questions.question: No
questions.explanation: 'Ei' means no and is also the negative verb in Finnish.

questions.question: It's nothing / No problem
questions.explanation: 'Ei se mitään' is a polite phrase meaning 'it's nothing' or 'no worries'.

questions.question: English (language)
questions.explanation: 'englanti' (lowercase) is the English language; capitalized 'Englanti' is the country England.

questions.question: England (country)
questions.explanation: Capitalized 'Englanti' is the country; lowercase 'englanti' is the language.

questions.question: What about / And (how about)
questions.explanation: 'Entä' is used to ask 'what about...?' or 'and how about...?'
questions.exampletranslate: I am Finnish. What about you?

questions.question: That (conjunction)
questions.explanation: 'Että' is a conjunction meaning 'that', linking clauses.
questions.example: Hän sanoo, että hän on naimaton.
questions.exampletranslate: He says that he is single.

questions.question: First name
questions.explanation: 'Etunimi' is the first name, from 'etu' (front) and 'nimi' (name).

questions.question: Fun / Nice
questions.explanation: 'Hauska' means fun, nice or pleasant; 'hauska tutustua' means 'nice to meet you'.

questions.question: They / Their
questions.explanation: 'He' is the third person plural pronoun (they); 'heidän' is the genitive (their).

questions.question: Hi / Hello
questions.explanation: 'Hei' is an informal greeting meaning hi or hello.

questions.question: Personal information / details
questions.explanation: 'Henkilötiedot' means personal information, from 'henkilö' (person) and 'tiedot' (data).
questions.exampletranslate: Fill in the personal information on the form.

questions.question: Personal identity code
questions.explanation: 'Henkilötunnus' is the Finnish personal identity code (like a social security number).
questions.exampletranslate: Write your personal identity code here.

questions.question: He / She (his / her)
questions.explanation: 'Hän' is the gender-neutral third person singular pronoun for people; 'hänen' is the genitive.

questions.question: Age
questions.explanation: 'Ikä' means age; its genitive form is 'iän'.

questions.question: And
questions.explanation: 'Ja' is the basic conjunction meaning 'and'.

questions.question: Someone
questions.explanation: 'Joku' means someone or somebody; its genitive is 'jonkun'.
questions.exampletranslate: Someone is calling on the phone.

questions.question: Canada
questions.explanation: 'Kanada' is the country Canada.

questions.question: Citizenship / Nationality
questions.explanation: 'Kansalaisuus' means citizenship or nationality.

questions.question: City
questions.explanation: 'Kaupunki' means city or town; its genitive is 'kaupungin'.

questions.question: Language
questions.explanation: 'Kieli' means language (and also tongue); its genitive is 'kielen'.

questions.question: Thanks / Thank you
questions.explanation: 'Kiitos' means thanks or thank you.

questions.question: To write
questions.explanation: 'Kirjoittaa' (type 1 verb) means to write.

questions.question: Home
questions.explanation: 'Koti' means home; its genitive is 'kodin'.

questions.question: How (in what manner)
questions.explanation: 'Kuinka' means how, often used like 'miten' (e.g. 'kuinka vanha' – how old).

questions.question: Who
questions.explanation: 'Kuka' means who; its genitive is 'kenen' (whose).

questions.question: Question
questions.explanation: 'Kysymys' means question; its genitive is 'kysymyksen'.

questions.question: Country / Land
questions.explanation: 'Maa' means country, land or ground; its genitive is 'maan'.

questions.question: We / Our
questions.explanation: 'Me' is the first person plural pronoun (we); 'meidän' is the genitive (our).

questions.question: Man
questions.explanation: 'Mies' means man (and also husband); its genitive is 'miehen'.

questions.question: What / Which
questions.explanation: 'Mikä' means what or which; its genitive is 'minkä'.

questions.question: How old (what age)
questions.explanation: 'Minkä ikäinen' literally means 'of what age', i.e. how old.

questions.question: What nationality
questions.explanation: 'Minkä maalainen' means 'from which country', i.e. what nationality.

questions.question: I / My
questions.explanation: 'Minä' is the first person singular pronoun (I); 'minun' is the genitive (my).

questions.question: Where
questions.explanation: 'Missä' means where (in what place), the inessive form of 'mikä'.

questions.question: How (in what way)
questions.explanation: 'Miten' means how, asking about manner or method.

questions.question: Neighbor
questions.explanation: 'Naapuri' means neighbor.

questions.question: Unmarried / Single
questions.explanation: 'Naimaton' means unmarried or single; its genitive is 'naimattoman'.

questions.question: Woman
questions.explanation: 'Nainen' means woman; its genitive is 'naisen'.

questions.question: Name
questions.explanation: 'Nimi' means name; its genitive is 'nimen'.

questions.question: Number
questions.explanation: 'Numero' means number.

questions.question: To see
questions.explanation: 'Nähdä' (type 2 verb) means to see; 'näen' is 'I see'.

questions.question: Here you are / Please (offering)
questions.explanation: 'Ole hyvä' means 'here you are', 'please' or 'you're welcome'.
questions.exampletranslate: Here is your coffee, you're welcome.

questions.question: To be
questions.explanation: 'Olla' (type 3 verb) means to be; 'olen' is 'I am'.

questions.question: Problem
questions.explanation: 'Ongelma' means problem.

questions.question: Teacher
questions.explanation: 'Opettaja' means teacher, from the verb 'opettaa' (to teach).

questions.question: To study
questions.explanation: 'Opiskella' (type 3 verb) means to study; 'opiskelen' is 'I study'.

questions.question: Address
questions.explanation: 'Osoite' means address; its genitive is 'osoitteen'.

questions.question: Postal code / Zip code
questions.explanation: 'Postinumero' means postal code or zip code.

questions.question: Post office town / postal locality
questions.explanation: 'Postitoimipaikka' is the town or locality named in a postal address.

questions.question: Telephone
questions.explanation: 'Puhelin' means telephone; its genitive is 'puhelimen'.

questions.question: Phone number
questions.explanation: 'Puhelinnumero' means phone number, from 'puhelin' and 'numero'.

questions.question: To speak
questions.explanation: 'Puhua' (type 1 verb) means to speak; 'puhun' is 'I speak'.

questions.question: Money
questions.explanation: 'Raha' means money.

questions.question: France
questions.explanation: 'Ranska' is the country France (and also the French language, lowercase).

questions.question: Likewise / Same to you
questions.explanation: 'Samoin' means likewise or 'same to you', e.g. replying to 'nice to meet you'.

questions.question: To say
questions.explanation: 'Sanoa' (type 1 verb) means to say; 'sanon' is 'I say'.

questions.question: It / That
questions.explanation: 'Se' means it or that; its genitive is 'sen'. In speech it can also replace 'hän'.

questions.question: You / Your (singular)
questions.explanation: 'Sinä' is the informal second person singular (you); 'sinun' is the genitive (your).

questions.question: Marital status
questions.explanation: 'Siviilisääty' means marital status (married, single, etc.).

questions.question: Surname / Last name
questions.explanation: 'Sukunimi' means surname or family name, from 'suku' (family) and 'nimi' (name).

questions.question: Gender / Sex
questions.explanation: 'Sukupuoli' means gender or sex; its genitive is 'sukupuolen'.

questions.question: Finnish (person)
questions.explanation: 'Suomalainen' means a Finn or Finnish (as a person/adjective).

questions.question: Finnish (language)
questions.explanation: 'suomi' (lowercase) is the Finnish language; capitalized 'Suomi' is the country.

questions.question: Finland (country)
questions.explanation: Capitalized 'Suomi' is the country Finland; lowercase 'suomi' is the language.

questions.question: Date of birth
questions.explanation: 'Syntymäaika' means date of birth, from 'syntymä' (birth) and 'aika' (time).
questions.exampletranslate: What is your date of birth?

questions.question: Email
questions.explanation: 'Sähköposti' means email, literally 'electric mail'.

questions.question: Email address
questions.explanation: 'Sähköpostiosoite' means email address, from 'sähköposti' and 'osoite'.

questions.question: House
questions.explanation: 'Talo' means house or building.
questions.exampletranslate: We live in a big house.

questions.question: To meet
questions.explanation: 'Tavata' (type 4 verb) means to meet; 'tapaan' is 'I meet'.

questions.question: You / Your (plural or formal)
questions.explanation: 'Te' is the plural/formal second person (you all, or polite you); 'teidän' is the genitive.

questions.question: Welcome
questions.explanation: 'Tervetuloa' means welcome.

questions.question: To get to know / get acquainted
questions.explanation: 'Tutustua' (type 1 verb) means to get to know or become acquainted; 'tutustun' is 'I get to know'.
questions.exampletranslate: I want to get to know you.

questions.question: To complete / fill in
questions.explanation: 'Täydentää' (type 1 verb) means to complete or fill in; 'täydennän' is 'I fill in'.

questions.question: New
questions.explanation: 'Uusi' means new; its genitive is 'uuden'.

questions.question: Wife
questions.explanation: 'Vaimo' means wife.

questions.question: Only
questions.explanation: 'Vain' means only or just.

questions.question: Old
questions.explanation: 'Vanha' means old; its genitive is 'vanhan'.

questions.question: Russia
questions.explanation: 'Venäjä' is the country Russia (and also the Russian language, lowercase).

questions.question: Russian (person)
questions.explanation: 'Venäläinen' means a Russian person (or Russian as an adjective).

questions.question: Year
questions.explanation: 'Vuosi' means year; its genitive is 'vuoden'.

questions.question: A little
questions.explanation: 'Vähän' means a little or a bit.

questions.question: The United States
questions.explanation: 'Yhdysvallat' means the United States; its genitive is 'Yhdysvaltojen'.
questions.exampletranslate: He lives in the United States.

questions.question: To understand
questions.explanation: 'Ymmärtää' (type 1 verb) means to understand; 'ymmärrän' is 'I understand'.

questions.question: Mother tongue / Native language
questions.explanation: 'Äidinkieli' means mother tongue, from 'äiti' (mother) and 'kieli' (language).
